input.task: Write the investment thesis and the recommendation on COSTCO WHOLESALE CORP /NEW (COST) from the two analysts' outputs.

overview.claim: Costco runs membership warehouses in the U.S., Puerto Rico and several other countries in North America, Asia, Europe and Oceania.
overview.quote: We are principally engaged in the operation of membership warehouses in the United States (U.S.) and Puerto Rico, Canada, Mexico, Japan, the United Kingdom (U.K.), Korea, Australia, Taiwan, China, Spain, France, Sweden, Iceland, and New Zealand.

overview.claim: Its model offers low prices on a limited selection of branded and private-label products to drive high sales volumes and fast inventory turnover.
overview.quote: We operate membership warehouses and e-commerce sites based on the concept that offering low prices on a limited selection of nationally-branded and private-label products in a wide range of categories will produce high sales volumes and rapid inventory turnover.

overview.claim: The company earns its operating cash mainly from merchandise sales and membership fees.
overview.quote: Our cash flow provided by operations is primarily from net sales and membership fees.

business_model.claim: The company reports three operating segments, U.S., Canadian and Other International, which use broadly the same operating model.
business_model.quote: Our operating models are generally the same across our U.S., Canadian, and Other International operating segments (see Note 11 to the consolidated financial statements included in Item 8 of this Report).

business_model.claim: Its customers are paid members, who numbered 84,100 thousand at the end of 2026, up from 81,000 thousand in 2025.
Executive members, who pay a higher fee, accounted for about 75.2% of worldwide net sales in 2026.
business_model.quote: The penetration of sales to Executive members represented approximately 75.2% of worldwide net sales in 2026.

business_model.claim: The company runs on thin merchandise margins, with a gross margin percentage of 11.09% in 2026.

competitive_position.claim: Costco operated 939 warehouses worldwide at the end of fiscal 2026, up from 914 a year earlier.
competitive_position.quote: Costco operated 939, 914, and 890 warehouses worldwide at August 30, 2026, August 31, 2025, and September 1, 2024.

competitive_position.claim: Member loyalty is high, with renewal rates of 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada and 89.8% worldwide at the end of 2026.
competitive_position.quote: Our member renewal rate was 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada and 89.8% worldwide at the end of 2026.

competitive_position.claim: The filing names Walmart, Target, Kroger and Amazon as significant U.S. general merchandise competitors.
competitive_position.quote: Walmart, Target, Kroger, and Amazon are among our significant general merchandise retail competitors in the U.S.

competitive_position.claim: Management sees higher tariffs as a threat that is more likely to hurt than help results.
competitive_position.quote: Higher tariffs are more likely to adversely impact rather than improve our results.

catalysts.claim: The company plans to open up to 33 new warehouses in fiscal 2027, including five relocations, after opening 28 in 2026.
catalysts.quote: We opened 28 new warehouses, including three relocations, in 2026, and plan to open up to 33 new warehouses, including five relocations, in 2027.

catalysts.claim: Management intends to raise capital expenditures to about $7,500 million in fiscal 2027 from $6,435 million in 2026.
catalysts.quote: In 2026, we spent $6,435 on capital expenditures, and it is our current intention to spend approximately $7,500 during fiscal 2027.

catalysts.claim: Management expects to keep increasing the sales penetration of its private-label items.
catalysts.quote: We expect to continue to increase the sales penetration of our private-label items.

catalysts.claim: Management says that growth in members, more Executive memberships and high renewal rates materially influence profitability.
catalysts.quote: The extent to which we achieve growth in our membership base, increase the penetration of Executive memberships, and sustain high renewal rates materially influences our profitability.

recent_developments.claim: Fiscal 2026 net sales rose 10.1 percent to $297.2 billion from $269.9 billion.
recent_developments.quote: Net sales for the fiscal year increased 10.1 percent, to $297.2 billion, from $269.9 billion last year.

recent_developments.claim: Fiscal 2026 net income was $9.226 billion, or $20.76 per diluted share, compared with $8.099 billion, or $18.21 per diluted share, a year earlier.
recent_developments.quote: Net income for the fiscal year was $9.226 billion, $20.76 per diluted share, compared to $8.099 billion, $18.21 per diluted share, last year.

recent_developments.claim: Fourth-quarter results included a non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share from IEEPA tariff refunds, net of partial reinvestment in member values.
recent_developments.quote: This year's fourth quarter was positively impacted by a non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share from IEEPA tariff refunds received in the quarter, less partial reinvestment of those refunds in increased member values.

recent_developments.claim: In April 2026 the Board raised the quarterly cash dividend from $1.30 to $1.47 per share.
recent_developments.quote: In April 2026, the Board of Directors increased our quarterly cash dividend from $1.30 to $1.47 per share.

financial_analyst.statement_analysis:
### COST: fiscal year ended 2026-08-30 (52 weeks, 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-30) compared with the prior year (2024-09-02 to 2025-08-31)

All figures come from 10-K 0000909832-26-000093, filed 2026-10-07, unless stated otherwise. Ratios were computed in code, and each one shows its arithmetic as given. Units are $ millions, except per share.

#### Growth
| Item | FY ended 2026-08-30 | FY ended 2025-08-31 | Growth | Arithmetic | XBRL tag |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total revenue | $303,154.0 million | $275,235.0 million | 10.14% | 303,154.0 / 275,235.0 - 1 | us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax |
| Operating income | $11,685.0 million | $10,383.0 million | 12.54% | 11,685.0 / 10,383.0 - 1 | us-gaap:OperatingIncomeLoss |
| Net income attributable to the company | $9,226.0 million | $8,099.0 million | 13.92% | 9,226.0 / 8,099.0 - 1 | us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss |
| Diluted EPS (GAAP) | $20.76 | $18.21 | 14.00% | 20.76 / 18.21 - 1 | us-gaap:EarningsPerShareDiluted |
| Cash from operations | $15,817.0 million | $13,335.0 million | 18.61% | 15,817.0 / 13,335.0 - 1 | us-gaap:NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities |
| Additions to property and equipment | $6,435.0 million | $5,498.0 million | 17.04% | 6,435.0 / 5,498.0 - 1 | us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment |

Each line grew faster than the line above it. Operating income grew 12.54% and net income grew 13.92%, both faster than revenue at 10.14%. Diluted EPS grew 14.00%, slightly faster than net income. The fiscal year EPS of $20.76 includes the fourth-quarter non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share from IEEPA tariff refunds (8-K 0000909832-26-000084, Exhibit 99.1, release sentence).

#### Margins
| Margin | FY ended 2026-08-30 | Arithmetic | FY ended 2025-08-31 | Arithmetic |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Operating margin | 3.85% | 11,685.0 / 303,154.0 | 3.77% | 10,383.0 / 275,235.0 |
| Net margin | 3.04% | 9,226.0 / 303,154.0 | 2.94% | 8,099.0 / 275,235.0 |

Both margins are thin, as expected for a membership warehouse model, and both rose year on year. Operating margin went from 3.77% to 3.85%, and net margin went from 2.94% to 3.04%.

#### Returns on equity
- **Return on average equity: 28.40%** = 9,226.0 / ((35,803.0 + 29,164.0) / 2).
  - Net income comes from us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss for FY2026.
  - Stockholders' equity is $35,803.0 million at 2026-08-30 and $29,164.0 million at 2025-08-31 (us-gaap:StockholdersEquity).
  - This uses average equity, not year-end equity.

#### Leverage
- **Debt to equity at 2026-08-30: 0.172** = (3,914.0 + 2,248.0) / 35,803.0.
  - Long-term debt excluding current maturities is $3,914.0 million (us-gaap:LongTermDebtNoncurrent).
  - Current portion is $2,248.0 million (us-gaap:LongTermDebtCurrent).
- **Debt to equity at 2025-08-31: 0.198** = (5,713.0 + 75.0) / 29,164.0.
- Leverage is low and fell over the year. Note the shift in maturity: the current portion of long-term debt rose from $75.0 million to $2,248.0 million, while noncurrent debt fell from $5,713.0 million to $3,914.0 million. A larger share of debt now falls due within the next year.
- This measure counts only long-term debt and its current portion. Lease liabilities are not in the context, so they are excluded.

#### Free cash flow
- **Free cash flow FY2026: $9,382.0M** = 15,817.0 - 6,435.0 (cash from operations minus additions to property and equipment).
- **Free cash flow FY2025: $7,837.0M** = 13,335.0 - 5,498.0.
- **Free cash flow growth: 19.71%** = (15,817.0 - 6,435.0) / (13,335.0 - 5,498.0) - 1.
- **Free cash flow margin: 3.09%** = (15,817.0 - 6,435.0) / 303,154.0.
- **Free cash flow / net income: 1.02** = (15,817.0 - 6,435.0) / 9,226.0.
- Cash conversion is full: free cash flow slightly exceeds net income. This holds even though capital spending grew 17.04%.
financial_analyst.latest_quarter:
### Fourth quarter: 16 weeks ended August 30, 2026

Source: 8-K accession 0000909832-26-000084, Item 2.02, Exhibit 99.1, accepted 2026-09-24 16:17:37 ET. Units are "(dollars in millions, except per share data) (unaudited)".

The fourth quarter is a **16-week** period, not 13 weeks. Column header: `16 Weeks Ended | 52 Weeks Ended / August 30, 2026 | August 31, 2025 | August 30, 2026 | August 31, 2025`.

#### Revenue
Release lines:
- `Net sales | $93,873 | $84,432 | $297,247 | $269,912`
- `Membership fees | 1,850 | 1,724 | 5,907 | 5,323`
- `Total revenue | 95,723 | 86,156 | 303,154 | 275,235`

- Quarter total revenue was $95,723 million, against $86,156 million in the same 16 weeks last year.
- **Growth: 11.10%** = 95,723 / 86,156 - 1 (the first two columns of the revenue line).
- The release's 52-week total revenue of 303,154 matches the 10-K figure.

#### GAAP diluted EPS
Release line, under the heading `NET INCOME PER COMMON SHARE:`:
- `Diluted | $6.75 | $5.87 | $20.76 | $18.21`

- Quarter GAAP diluted EPS was $6.75, against $5.87 in the same quarter last year.
- **Growth: 14.99%** = 6.75 / 5.87 - 1 (the release's first two columns).

The release states:
> "Net income for the fourth quarter was $2.998 billion, $6.75 per diluted share, compared to $2.610 billion, $5.87 per diluted share, last year. This year's fourth quarter was positively impacted by a non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share from IEEPA tariff refunds received in the quarter, less partial reinvestment of those refunds in increased member values."

The GAAP $6.75 therefore includes a one-off benefit of $0.15 per diluted share. No figure excluding that benefit is computed here.

### Peer comparison on total revenue and GAAP operating income (operating margin = operating income / total revenue)

| Company | Fiscal year end | Total revenue | Operating income | Operating margin | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Costco (COST) | 2026-08-30 | $303,154.0 million | $11,685.0 million | 3.85% = 11,685.0 / 303,154.0 | 10-K 0000909832-26-000093; us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax, us-gaap:OperatingIncomeLoss |
| Walmart (WMT) | 2026-01-31 | $713,163.0 million | $29,825.0 million | 4.18% = 29,825.0 / 713,163.0 | 10-K 0000104169-26-000055; us-gaap:Revenues, us-gaap:OperatingIncomeLoss |
| Target (TGT) | 2026-01-31 | $104,780.0 million | $5,117.0 million | 4.88% = 5,117.0 / 104,780.0 | 10-K 0000027419-26-000016; us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax, us-gaap:OperatingIncomeLoss |
| BJ's Wholesale (BJ) | 2026-01-31 | $21,457.3 million | $816.6 million | 3.81% = 816.6 / 21,457.3 | 10-K 0001531152-26-000007; us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax, us-gaap:OperatingIncomeLoss |

**Notes**
- **Fiscal years differ.** COST's year ends 2026-08-30. The three peers' years end 2026-01-31, seven months earlier.
- **Revenue tags differ.**
  - All four use total revenue, not net sales.
  - COST, TGT and BJ report under us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax.
  - WMT reports under us-gaap:Revenues.
  - For COST, total revenue includes membership fees.
- **Scale.** COST's total revenue of $303,154.0 million is smaller than WMT's $713,163.0 million. It is larger than TGT's $104,780.0 million and BJ's $21,457.3 million.
- **Operating margin.**
  - COST's 3.85% is below WMT's 4.18% and TGT's 4.88%.
  - It is about level with its closest format peer, BJ, at 3.81%.
  - The context holds no peer growth, return, leverage or P/E figures, so peers are compared on operating margin only.
financial_analyst.valuation:
### Valuation

- **P/E: 47.8** = 992.13 / 20.76 (price / diluted EPS).
  - The price of $992.13 was supplied with --price. The context gives no date for this price, so its date is not stated.
  - EPS is FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS of $20.76 (us-gaap:EarningsPerShareDiluted, 10-K 0000909832-26-000093, period 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-30).
- **What the ratios say about value:**
  - At 47.8 times GAAP earnings, the price embeds a high multiple relative to the earnings growth just reported: diluted EPS grew 14.00% for the year and 14.99% in the 16-week fourth quarter.
  - The underlying business quality is strong:
    - return on average equity of 28.40%;
    - debt to equity of 0.172;
    - free cash flow of $9,382.0M, or 1.02 times net income;
    - operating margin up from 3.77% to 3.85%.
  - The FY2026 EPS includes the non-recurring $0.15 per diluted share tariff-refund benefit in Q4. The P/E on GAAP EPS is therefore slightly flattered relative to recurring earnings.
  - The context has no shares outstanding, market capitalisation or peer P/E figures. A free-cash-flow yield and a relative multiple comparison cannot be produced.
- No recommendation is given; another role makes that call.
definitions: Revenue: total revenue (net sales plus membership fees), tagged us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax, rather than net sales alone. Peers are also compared on total revenue, with WMT reported under us-gaap:Revenues.
Return on equity: return on average equity, using the mean of stockholders' equity at 2026-08-30 and 2025-08-31, rather than year-end equity.
EPS: GAAP diluted EPS throughout ($20.76 for the year, $6.75 for the quarter). No adjusted EPS excluding the $0.15 tariff-refund benefit is used.
Net income: net income attributable to the company (us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss).
Debt: long-term debt excluding current maturities plus the current portion of long-term debt. Lease liabilities are excluded because they are not in the context.
Free cash flow: cash from operations minus additions to property and equipment.
Latest quarter: the 16 weeks ended August 30, 2026, compared with the 16 weeks ended August 31, 2025, as presented in the earnings release.

output.thesis:
**Hold: an excellent business at a full price.**

- **Strong operations.** Costco's model is working. Total revenue grew 10.14% to $303,154.0 million. Diluted EPS grew 14.00% to $20.76. Operating margin rose from 3.77% to 3.85%.
- **Loyal, growing members.** Paid members rose from 81,000 thousand to 84,100 thousand. Renewal rates were 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada and 89.8% worldwide.
- **High-quality balance sheet and cash flow.** Return on average equity is 28.40% and debt to equity is 0.172. Free cash flow of $9,382.0M is 1.02 times net income.
- **The price already reflects this.** At a P/E of **47.8**, the stock trades at a high multiple relative to EPS growth of 14.00% for the year and 14.99% in the 16-week fourth quarter.
- **Earnings slightly flattered.** FY2026 EPS includes a non-recurring $0.15 per diluted share benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds, so the multiple on recurring earnings is a little higher than it looks.
- **What is missing.** The context has no peer P/E, market capitalisation or free-cash-flow yield. Neither a clear discount nor a clear excess can be shown, so Hold rather than Buy or Sell.
output.what_would_change_it: A price decline that brings the P/E well below 47.8 would move the call to Buy, provided EPS growth holds near 14.00% and renewal rates stay at 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada and 89.8% worldwide. A drop in those renewal rates, or operating margin slipping back from 3.85% toward 3.77%, would move it toward Sell at the current multiple.
strategic_recommendations: Watch membership health at each report: paid members of 84,100 thousand, a worldwide renewal rate of 89.8%, and Executive members driving about 75.2% of worldwide net sales. Management states these factors "materially influence our profitability."

Track whether the planned rise in capital expenditures to approximately $7,500 in fiscal 2027 (from $6,435) and up to 33 new warehouses keeps free cash flow near 1.02 times net income, and how the current portion of long-term debt of $2,248.0 million (up from $75.0 million) is refinanced or repaid.

Judge future EPS growth against the 47.8 P/E without the non-recurring $0.15 per diluted share tariff-refund benefit, given management's view that "Higher tariffs are more likely to adversely impact rather than improve our results."
